use_case_name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

claims.content: C2 JU transmits available IFF/SIF Modes I, II, and III Codes in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI=0) messages to exchange IFF/SIF transponder data.

scope_contract.goal_statement: C2 JU transmits available IFF/SIF Modes I, II, and III Codes in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI=0) messages to exchange IFF/SIF transponder data.

claims.content: C2 JU
IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) are available to the system.

The use case is triggered when IFF/SIF transponder data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) becomes available to C2 JU for exchange via J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI=0) messages, when an R² unit reports a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report, or when an operator transmits a J7.5 (ACT=2) IFF/SIF Update Request.
IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) is available to C2 JU for transmission in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI=0) messages.
C2 JU determines that it is the JU with R² and is therefore responsible for reporting IFF/SIF data in conjunction with periodic surveillance data.
C2 JU transmits the available IFF/SIF Modes I, II, and III Codes in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI=0) messages.
C2 JU periodically transmits IFF/SIF surveillance data (Modes I, II, and III codes) in J3.1/J3.5 messages to report valid data held for the track.

Alternatively, when the R² unit reports a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report, data updating may occur spontaneously as receiving units holding valid nonzero data respond per the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix; alternatively, the C2 JU may initiate a J7.5 (ACT=2) IFF/SIF Update Request via operator action, upon which R² units respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message and NonR² units holding valid local data respond with a J7.5 (ACT=1) message.
Diverges from Step 3: The C2 JU may transmit a Special Code message (J7.5 with ACT=3) to exchange special-meaning IFF/SIF codes.
Diverges from Step 3: If locally derived IFF/SIF data differs from IFF/SIF data that was being reported in the PPLI message, the locally derived data shall be reported.

Diverges from Step 4: Instead of continuing the periodic J3.1/J3.5 report, the C2 JU (initiated by operator action) transmits a J7.5 (ACT=2) IFF/SIF Update Request message to request updated transponder data from another unit; receiving units respond by transmitting their local data codes.

Diverges from Step 4: Instead of only periodically reporting held data, the C2 JU transmits a J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report to report a difference in accordance with the Difference Resolution Matrix; this may be initiated by operator action at any time.

Diverges from Step 4: In a required J3.XC1 surveillance data report, the R² unit reports a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes; receiving units holding valid nonzero data respond as required by the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix.

Diverges from Step 4: Instead of continuing to transmit valid data in the periodic J3 message, a JU with R² initiates a J7.5 (ACT=0) message to clear one or more modes on the specified track; this results in no IFF/SIF data being held on that track and causes the JU to stop transmitting the periodic J3 message containing the continuation word for that track.

Diverges from Step 4: On receipt of a J7.5 (ACT=0) message, the C2 JU automatically sets the designated mode(s) for the specified track to the No Data status; acceptance or rejection of a Mode IV Clear message may be automatic or by operator determination.
Diverges from Step 4: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, they may manually update local data or verify automatic inputs to resolve the difference.

missing_aspects: The claim states the JU 'instead of transmitting Modes I, II, and III Codes in J3.1/J3.5 (PTI=0) messages', but the cited evidence card EC-AF-001 only supports that the JU 'may transmit' the Special Code message; it does not explicitly state this action replaces or excludes the transmission of standard Mode I/II/III codes in other messages.

claims.content: Diverges from main_flow step 3: If no valid code is currently held for the subject local or remote track/mode, a 'No Data' condition exists and the applicable Mode Code field is reported as zeroes. Exit: the zero-valued Mode Code is transmitted as the No Data report.

Diverges from main_flow step 4: If the C2 JU with R² transmits a J3.XC1 message with a 'NO DATA' report (value 0) for one or more modes while local nonzero IFF/SIF is held, receiving units holding valid nonzero IFF/SIF respond in accordance with the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix.

Diverges from main_flow step 4: If C2 JU is a receiving unit and locally entered IFF/SIF data changes from zero to nonzero or from nonzero to another nonzero value, or it receives a J3.XC1 'NO DATA' report on one or more mode/code while local nonzero IFF/SIF is held, it may report the difference via J7.5 (ACT=1) in accordance with the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix. Exit: C2 JU initiates the J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report.

Diverges from main_flow step 4: If C2 JU receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the operator shall have the following manual actions available for attempting resolution: (1) update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) initiate J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear IFF/SIF message; (3) initiate J7.5 (ACT=1) IFF/SIF Difference Report; (4) change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) decorrelate local data from remote data, causing assignment of a new track number to local data; or (6) clear the operator alert. Exit: the operator selects one of the available manual resolution actions.

Diverges from main_flow step 4: If the C2 JU with R² identifies an ID conflict, the operator is alerted and local ID data continues to be reported in the appropriate surveillance message with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 1; the conflict is resolved by manual means. Exit: reporting continues with the indicator set to 1 until manual resolution.

Diverges from main_flow step 2: If the C2 JU is a NonR² JU and an IFF/SIF conflict is indicated, it inhibits transmission of J7.0 (ACT=1) until the surveillance message is received with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 0. Exit: the inhibition is lifted when the Identity Difference Indicator is received as 0.

missing_aspects: Explicit post-action continuation after the data-conflict-alert manual resolution actions is not documented in the provided evidence.
Exception handling for the J7.5 (ACT=2) Update Request path is not covered by the provided evidence.
Explicit evidence that the response path is specifically the 'J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report'

claims.content: The IFF/SIF transponder data has been successfully exchanged in the applicable J-series message.
Upon successful exchange of IFF/SIF data via a J7.5 (ACT=2) Update Request message, the receiving units have responded by transmitting their local data codes.

After successful transmission and acceptance of a J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear IFF/SIF message, the designated mode(s) for the specified track have been set to No Data status on all receiving JUs, and periodic J3 transmissions containing continuation words for that track have ceased.
After successful completion of a J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report transmission, the reported difference has been communicated to relevant units.

missing_aspects: Postcondition state for the J7.5 (ACT=3) Special Code exchange variant is not covered by the available postcondition evidence.
Postcondition state for Unique Mode II Code Protection is not covered by the available postcondition evidence.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The main flow only describes J3.1/J3.5 (PTI=0) transmission of available/valid IFF/SIF data. It contains no J7.5 actions, so the postconditions for the J7.5 (ACT=2) Update Request, J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear, and J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report cannot be reached from the main flow. The same omission also leaves the J7.5 ACT=2 trigger path without a continuing main-flow sequence. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Evidence supports No Data reported as zeroes in the applicable Mode Code field, but does not specify transmission for 'required modes' lacking data.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The trigger includes the case where an R² unit reports a No Data status (value 0) for one or more required IFF/SIF modes, but the main flow only handles available/valid data and never reports No Data (value 0) in J3.1/J3.5 messages. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Evidence supports No Data reported as zeroes in the applicable Mode Code field, but does not specify transmission for 'required modes' lacking data.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 4 lists six manual resolution actions and exits with 'the operator selects one of the available manual resolution actions', but it does not state what happens after that selection. It does not return to a main_flow step, terminate/hand off, or reach a terminal failure/prevention state, so the branch lacks a clear outcome. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit exception-flow exit/recovery after the operator selects one of the manual resolution actions; cited cards support the available actions and some action effects but not an exit step.))

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger and Main Flow require C2 JU to be the R² reporting unit for the IFF/SIF exchange; Main Flow step 2 confirms that R² responsibility is a pre-existing role assignment rather than an outcome of the flow. Preconditions only assert IFF/SIF data availability, so this required external state is missing. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Evidence does not identify the C2 JU specifically as the R² holder; 'C2 JU' is unsupported added detail.; The phrase 'track/report' is not supported by the cited card, which refers to reporting IFF/SIF data in conjunction with periodic surveillance data.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Postconditions assert successful J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear and J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report exchanges, but neither the Trigger nor the Main Flow includes those messages. The Main Flow only transmits J3.1/J3.5 periodic IFF/SIF data, so these postconditions are unreachable and appear to belong to separate use cases. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The main flow covers periodic J3.1/J3.5 transmission, No Data handling, and J7.5 (ACT=2) update requests, but contains no step that transmits or accepts a J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear IFF/SIF message. Therefore the postcondition that modes have been set to No Data and periodic J3 transmissions cease after an ACT=0 Clear cannot be reached from the narrated behavior.

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The trigger (and main flow step 2) require C2 JU to be the unit with R² before it can report IFF/SIF data in J3.1/J3.5 messages, but the Preconditions slot only states that IFF/SIF data is available. The R² role/responsibility is an external state that must already hold for the primary actor to initiate the J3.1/J3.5 exchange path.

inconsistency_hints: Goal is too broad / conflates multiple flows: its scope_contract lists J7.5 (ACT=2) special-meaning code exchange as in-scope and names five IFF/SIF functional areas, but main_flow only covers R² periodic transmission of Modes I, II, and III Codes in J3.1/J3.5 (PTI=0). The J7.5 special-meaning exchange is not in main_flow, and the goal's own missing_aspects note that no evidence supports the J7.5 (ACT=2) usage.

The Trigger includes an R² No Data status report and an operator-transmitted J7.5 (ACT=2) Update Request as entry events, but the Main Flow restarts with J3.1/J3.5 transmission of available IFF/SIF codes and never reports No Data or processes the Update Request. For two of the three trigger alternatives, the Main Flow is a different scenario rather than a continuation.
